papers.title_zh: 益生菌作为缓解禽类病毒感染的策略:免疫调节机制与治疗潜力
papers.source_body_en: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions. Probiotics have gained attention as a promising strategy to combat these viral infections due to their potential in enhancing immune responses and establishing a healthy gut microbiome. A literature search was carried out on Google Scholar, Scopus and PubMed using key search terms, such as 'probiotics', 'Lactobacillus', 'acidophilus', 'poultry', 'viral infections', 'Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV)' and other relevant terms. Inclusion criteria for manuscripts used were based on the relevance to probiotic-based interventions in poultry, the focus on immunological mechanisms and the examination of viral pathogens commonly found in West African poultry farming systems. This review explores the role of probiotics in mitigating the effects of NDV, AIV and IBV in poultry, focusing on their immunomodulatory effects and antiviral mechanisms. Lactobacillus acidophilus, L. plantarum have shown an interesting promise in countering NDV infections by modulating immunological parameters and enhancing antibody responses. Similarly, these probiotics have exhibited antiviral activity against AIV, promoting immune activation and reducing viral loads. plantarum have emerged as potential adjuvants for IBV vaccines, improving antibody responses and humoural immunity.
papers.abstract_zh: 禽类病毒感染仍然是禽类养殖业中的持续挑战,导致显著的经济损失并可能对人类健康构成潜在威胁。涉及病原体的病毒感染频率不断上升,例如传染性支气管炎病毒(IBV)、新城疫病毒(NDV)和禽流感病毒(AIV),凸显了对有效干预措施的迫切需求。由于益生菌在增强免疫应答和建立健康肠道微生物群方面具有潜力,它们已成为一种有前景的策略,用于对抗这些病毒感染。通过在Google Scholar、Scopus和PubMed上使用关键搜索词,如'益生菌'、'乳酸杆菌'、'嗜酸乳杆菌'、'禽类'、'病毒感染'、'新城疫病毒(NDV)'及其他相关术语进行了文献检索。所选文献的纳入标准基于其与禽类益生菌干预措施的相关性、对免疫机制的关注以及对西非禽类养殖系统中常见病毒病原体的分析。本综述探讨了益生菌在减轻NDV、AIV和IBV对禽类影响中的作用,重点在于其免疫调节效应和抗病毒机制。嗜酸乳杆菌(Lactobacillus acidophilus)和植物乳杆菌(L. plantarum)在调节免疫参数和增强抗体反应方面显示出对抗NDV感染的有趣前景。同样,这些益生菌在对抗AIV方面也表现出抗病毒活性,促进免疫激活并降低病毒载量。植物乳杆菌在应对IBV病毒感染方面已显示出潜在的辅助作用,改善抗体反应和体液免疫。

papers.title: AEX-1: A Vero cell variant with enhanced permissiveness for influenza virus replication.
papers.abstract: Background Continuous cell substrates with improved permissiveness for influenza virus replication are of considerable interest for vaccine development and manufacturing. Vero cells have an excellent regulatory track record; however, their relatively low influenza virus productivity limits their broader application. Methods We developed the AEX-1 cell line by co-cultivating Vero cells with chicken embryo amniotic membrane fragments. Cellular morphology, intracellular acidification, influenza virus replication, transcriptomic profile, genetic stability, and tumorigenicity were evaluated. Results AEX-1 cells displayed distinct morphology and enhanced endosomal/lysosomal acidification compared with parental Vero cells. At 72 h post-infection, a commonly used harvest time for influenza vaccine virus production, AEX-1 cells produced higher infectious titres of WHO-recommended egg-derived A/Sydney/5/2021 (H1N1)pdm09-like and B/Austria/1359417/2021 vaccine viruses, with titres approaching those obtained in embryonated chicken eggs and exceeding Vero cell yields by 0.9-1.7 log 10 EID 50 /ml. No replication advantage was observed for the egg-derived A/Croatia/10136RV/2023 (H3N2) vaccine virus, carrying the egg-adaptive HA G53D substitution, or for the egg-derived A/duck/Vietnam/NCVD-1584/2012 (H5N1) vaccine strain. However, the A/Darwin/9/2021-like Vero-derived primary isolate A/Austria/1516645/2022 (H3N2), lacking G53D, reached infectious titres up to 3.0 log 10 TCID 50 /ml higher than in Vero and 2.3 log 10 TCID 50 /ml higher than in MDCK cells. H1N1 UniFluVec-based influenza virus vectors also replicated efficiently in AEX-1 cells. Transcriptomic analysis revealed changes in genes involved in proton transport, vesicular acidification, and intracellular pH regulation. AEX-1 remained genetically stable after prolonged passaging and showed no evidence of increased tumorigenicity in vitro or in vivo. Conclusions Enhanced intracellular acidification may contribute to improved influenza virus replication in AEX-1 cells, suggesting that modulation of endosomal acidification may provide a rational strategy for developing improved cell substrates for influenza vaccine production.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在开发一种对流感病毒复制具有增强允许性的细胞系,以提高疫苗的生产,解决流感疫苗开发中对更优细胞基质的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及通过将Vero细胞与鸡胚胎羊膜碎片共培养来开发AEX-1细胞,并将其与亲本Vero细胞及其他细胞系进行比较评估。
elements_zh.methods: 评估了AEX-1细胞的细胞形态、细胞内酸化、流感病毒复制、转录组谱、遗传稳定性以及致瘤性。
elements_zh.main_results: AEX-1细胞表现出增强的流感病毒复制能力,其产生的流感疫苗病毒感染滴度高于Vero细胞,滴度接近鸡卵中获得的水平。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,AEX-1细胞中增强的细胞内酸化可能有助于流感病毒的复制,这表明调节囊泡酸化可能为开发更优的流感疫苗生产细胞基质提供合理的策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,AEX-1细胞可能成为流感疫苗生产的重要工具,有望提高疫苗病毒复制的效率和产量。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括需要进一步验证AEX-1细胞在大规模生产中的表现,以及在疫苗生产中缺乏与其他细胞系的直接比较。

papers.title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
papers.abstract: Abstract Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study benchmarks four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing, including custom and off-the-shelf methods.
analysis.methods: Ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets.
analysis.main_results: Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The custom panel provides needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the development of genomic surveillance tools for avian influenza A viruses in wastewater, supporting improved monitoring of low-abundance seasonal variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes, and the evidence is based on abstract-only data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the effectiveness of four targeted enrichment methods for whole-genome sequencing of influenza A viruses (IAV) in wastewater. The research highlights the challenges of IAV detection in low-abundance environments and introduces a custom HA tiled-amplicon panel as a sensitive, fast, and cost-effective tool for monitoring seasonal variants. The study demonstrates that ultrafiltration-based virus concentration outperforms other methods in wastewater samples. The custom panel is suitable for known subtypes but has limitations due to reliance on conserved primer-binding sites. The findings suggest that these methods can improve genomic surveillance of avian influenza in wastewater, though the evidence is based on abstract-only data. The study contributes to the development of tools for IAV monitoring, emphasizing the importance of tailored approaches for low-abundance variants.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 甲型流感病毒(IAV)仍然是一个持续的One Health威胁,从废水中进行全基因组测序提供了一种有前景的监测工具。然而,IAV在废水中的丰度较低,使得测序变得困难。我们对四种适用于多亚型全基因组 IAV测序的靶向富集方法进行了基准测试,包括定制和现成的方法。我们的定制HA tiled-amplicon面板具有灵敏、快速和成本效益的特点,使其适用于监测已知亚型低丰度的季节性变种,尽管其依赖于保守且完整的引物结合位点,这限制了引物设计的亚型数量。一种已发表的通用amplicon方法可针对所有IAV亚型,但由于依赖于完整的基因组片段,在废水样本中表现不佳。同时,探针捕获方法对RNA降解具有较强的抵抗力。在实际废水样本中,我们的定制探针面板能够从循环中的H1N1、H3N2、H5N1中回收全基因组信号,包括在dPCR检测受限的样本中验证的H5N1 2.3.4.4b读数。然而,探针捕获方法通常比amplicon方法更昂贵且劳动密集。在所有四种测序方法、两种废水基质以及大多数spike-in和内源性病毒目标中,基于超滤的病毒浓缩方法始终优于大体积直接提取。综上所述,这些基准测试比较和定制面板为在常规废水监测中实施IAV基因组测序提供了必要的信息。

strengthening collaboration, preparedness & response Home Public health events Avian influenza A(H5N1) human cases – United States – 2024-2026 19 October 2026 Avian influenza A(H5N1) human cases – United States – 2024-2026 Outbreaks Active 19 October 2026 Key facts On 15 October 2026, a confirmed human case of avian influenza A(H5N1) was reported in a resident of Yakima County, Washington state, USA, following occupational exposure to infected dairy cattle at a local dairy farm. The case had mild symptoms and was not hospitalised. Since 1 April 2024, and as of 15 October 2026, 72 human cases with avian influenza have been reported from 13 states in the United States (US). Of these, 42 were individuals exposed to dairy cattle known or presumed to be infected with A(H5N1) and 24 were workers exposed to outbreaks of HPAI A(H5) at poultry farms. Three people had no known animal exposure and three had exposure to other animals, such as backyard flocks, wild birds, or other mammals. According to the US CDC, the risk from A(H5N1) viruses to the general population remains low, while the risk to individuals in contact with potentially infected animals, contaminated surfaces or fluids is considered moderate to high. ECDC is closely following the situation and is in close contact with Back to threats overview Page contents Overview Update: On 15 October 2026, a confirmed human case of avian influenza A(H5N1) was reported in a resident of Yakima County, Washington state, USA, following occupational exposure to infected dairy cattle at a local dairy farm (press release). The case experienced mild illness, was not hospitalised, and is currently isolating at home. Public health authorities have initiated contact tracing and symptom monitoring of close contacts to assess any potential onward transmission. No evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission has been identified. analysis_zh.location_and_population: 暴发在美国13个州被报告,包括华盛顿州、加利福尼亚州、科罗拉多州、密歇根州、内华达州、德克萨斯州、爱荷华州、俄亥俄州、俄勒冈州、威斯康星州、路易斯安那州、怀俄明州和密苏里州。受影响人群包括奶牛工人、家禽农场工人以及接触家养禽类、野生鸟类或其他哺乳动物的个体。
analysis_zh.event: 2026年10月15日,美国华盛顿州雅基马县报告了一例禽流感 A(H5N1)确诊病例,该病例与职业性接触感染奶牛有关。自2024年4月1日起,已报告72例人类病例,包括一例死亡,且未发现持续的人际传播传播。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 截至2026年10月15日,美国已报告72例禽流感 A(H5N1)人类病例,其中42例与奶牛接触有关,24例与家禽农场暴发有关。3例涉及接触其他动物,另有3例无已知动物接触。美国CDC表示,对一般人群的风险仍较低,但对于与感染动物或污染环境有密切或长期接触的个体,风险中等至较高。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 公共卫生部门已开始对密切接触者进行接触追踪和症状监测。美国CDC和ECDC正在合作监测情况,ECDC强调需要加强监测、对暴露人员进行检测以及传播流行病学情况的沟通。对一般人群的风险评估被认为是较低的,而对于职业暴露人群,风险则为低至中等。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Tuesday, October 20, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Poultry-exposed people around Poyang Lake showed varied avian influenza antibody reactivity, 2018–2025 by October 20, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Seven Years of Blood Tests Reveal Quiet Avian Flu Exposure Around Poyang Lake Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A cross-sectional serological surveillance study of occupationally exposed people around Poyang Lake found that hemagglutination-inhibition antibody reactivity to seven avian influenza virus subtypes varied by subtype, surveillance location and year between 2018 and 2025. The study analyzed 2,437 valid serum samples, including 1,599 from Jiujiang and 838 from Nanchang. Participants were backyard poultry keepers, their household members and live poultry market workers with direct poultry contact. The findings show antibody reactivity in the sampled population but do not, by themselves, establish subtype-specific human infection or local circulation of the viruses. The study’s abstract reports that 108 samples, or 4.43%, met the predefined positivity threshold for H5N6, while 107, or 4.39%, met the threshold for H9N2. During 2018–2020, 25 of 914 samples (2.74%) met the threshold for H7N9. From 2021 through 2025, 22 of 1,523 samples (1.44%) met the threshold for H3N8, including nine of 100 samples collected in Nanchang in the 2024 surveillance year (9.00%). Four of 1,523 samples (0.26%) met the threshold for H10N3, and all four were from Jiujiang in 2024. For H5N8, four of 314 samples (1.27%) met the threshold in 2020. None of the 600 samples tested for H5N1 in the 2024 and 2025 surveillance years met its predefined threshold. Discover more Shop Bird Supplies Identify Plants Book a Safari Samples were collected annually during winter and spring at surveillance sites in Nanchang County and in Duchang and Wuning counties, Jiujiang, Jiangxi Province. The National Influenza Center performed hemagglutination-inhibition assays using test antigens representing H5N6, H9N2, H7N9, H3N8, H10N3, H5N8 and H5N1. Positivity was defined as a titre of at least 1:20 for H3N8, H5N8, H5N1, H7N9 and H10N3, and at least 1:40 for H5N6 and H9N2. The abstract identifies peaks in H5N6 positivity in Jiujiang in 2021 and Nanchang in 2022, and in H9N2 positivity in Jiujiang in 2021 and Nanchang in 2023. It also identifies the H3N8 finding in Nanchang and the H10N3 finding in Jiujiang in the 2024 surveillance year as warranting further investigation. Discover more Get Cold Relief Study Biology Buy Fresh Poultry Manage Livestock Because this was an observational, cross-sectional study, the results describe antibody reactivity among selected occupationally exposed participants rather than clinically diagnosed infections. The number of samples tested differed among subtypes, locations and years, limiting direct comparisons across those groups. The article is presented in an accepted, citable version that the publisher says may undergo further edits before replacement by the final Version of Record. The authors concluded that continued serological surveillance, interpreted alongside poultry and environmental virological data, may inform risk assessment. The findings show antibody reactivity in the sampled population but do not, by themselves, establish subtype-specific human infection or local circulation of the viruses. The study’s abstract reports that 108 samples, or 4.43%, met the predefined positivity threshold for H5N6, while 107, or 4.39%, met the threshold for H9N2. During 2018–2020, 25 of 914 samples (2.74%) met the threshold for H7N9. From 2021 through 2025, 22 of 1,523 samples (1.44%) met the threshold for H3N8, including nine of 100 samples collected in Nanchang in the 2024 surveillance year (9.00%). Four of 1,523 samples (0.26%) met the threshold for H10N3, and all four were from Jiujiang in 2024. For H5N8, four of 314 samples (1.27%) met the threshold in 2020. None of the 600 samples tested for H5N1 in the 2024 and 2025 surveillance years met its predefined threshold. The National Influenza Center performed hemagglutination-inhibition assays using test antigens representing H5N6, H9N2, H7N9, H3N8, H10N3, H5N8 and H5N1. Positivity was defined as a titre of at least 1:20 for H3N8, H5N8, H5N1, H7N9 and H10N3, and at least 1:40 for H5N6 and H9N2. The abstract identifies peaks in H5N6 positivity in Jiujiang in 2021 and Nanchang in 2022, and in H9N2 positivity in Jiujiang in 2021 and Nanchang in 2023. It also identifies the H3N8 finding in Nanchang and the H10N3 finding in Jiujiang in the 2024 surveillance year as warranting further investigation. news.content_zh: 一项横断面血清学研究于2018年至2025年间在中国江西省鄱阳湖周边地区进行,发现接触禽类人群对禽流感病毒亚型表现出不同的抗体反应。该研究包括来自南昌县以及都昌和武宁县的2,437份血清样本,样本来自散养禽类饲养者、其家庭成员以及活禽市场工作人员。观察到的抗体阳性率分别为H5N6(4.43%)、H9N2(4.39%)、H7N9(2018–2020年为2.74%)和H3N8(2021–2025年为1.44%)。研究结果并未确认特定亚型的人类感染或病毒在当地循环。国家流感中心进行了血凝抑制试验,作者建议继续进行监测血清学研究,并结合禽类和环境的病毒学数据进行风险评估。研究指出,不同亚型、地点和年份的样本数量存在差异,限制了直接比较。这些结果基于抗体反应,而非临床诊断,文章以接受发表、可引用的版本呈现,可能在正式出版前进行进一步修改。

Latest Current Affairs - 2026-2027 Discover more Find Gov Offices Prep for Tests Book Freight H5N1 avian influenza was confirmed in water birds at Arignar Anna Zoological Park, also known as Vandalur Zoo, in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, confirmed the infection on 2 October 2026. Seven water birds died between 3 and 9 October. Avian Influenza and H5N1 Avian influenza is an infectious disease caused by influenza A viruses that primarily affect birds. The H and N in the designation H5N1 refer to the virus surface proteins haemagglutinin and neuraminidase; the numerals identify their subtypes. H5N1 is one subtype of avian influenza A virus. Wild water birds can carry avian influenza viruses, and infection may spread among birds through contaminated secretions or environments. Bird Mortality at Vandalur Zoo The seven deceased birds comprised four painted storks, one grey pelican, one grey heron and one oriental darter. The birds were housed in the zoo’s Vedanthangal enclosure. Zoo officials cordoned off the affected area after the first bird died on 3 October. No further bird deaths or signs of illness had been reported since 9 October, and the zoo director described the outbreak as likely over. Biosecurity and Preventive Measures The zoo closed to visitors on 22 and 23 October 2026 to allow intensive sanitisation, reinforce biosecurity and monitor the affected area. Measures included disinfection, sanitisation and restricted access to the affected zone. Water birds were given oral antibiotics, herbal antiviral medicines, immunostimulants and liver supplements. Biosecurity measures in animal facilities include controlling movement between enclosures and preventing the transfer of infection by people, equipment or contaminated materials. Important Facts for Exams H5N1 is an influenza A virus subtype named for its haemagglutinin 5 and neuraminidase 1 proteins. NIHSAD is located in Bhopal and confirmed the infection at Vandalur Zoo. Arignar Anna Zoological Park is located at Vandalur in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Painted storks, grey pelicans, grey herons and oriental darters were among the birds that died. Vandalur Zoo is also known as Arignar Anna Zoological Park. H5N1 confirmation led to a two-day visitor closure on 22 and 23 October 2026. analysis_en.event: H5N1 avian influenza was confirmed in water birds at Vandalur Zoo, reported by the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Seven water birds died between 3 and 9 October 2026. The outbreak is described as likely over by the zoo director. No human infections or broader community impact were reported.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The zoo implemented biosecurity measures, including disinfection, sanitisation, restricted access, and closure to visitors for two days. The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases confirmed the infection, and the zoo director assessed the outbreak as likely over.

news.title_zh: H5N1 禽流感 在万达尔动物园被确认 - GK 今日
news.source_body_en: H5N1 avian influenza was confirmed in water birds at Vandalur Zoo in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on 2 October 2026, with seven birds dying between 3 and 9 October. The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal verified the infection. The zoo cordoned off the affected area and closed to visitors on 22 and 23 October to enforce biosecurity measures, including disinfection and restricted access. The zoo director noted the outbreak as likely over after no further deaths or illness signs were reported. No human infections or broader community impact were mentioned in the evidence. The affected birds were housed in the Vedanthangal enclosure, which included painted storks, grey pelicans, grey herons, and oriental darters. The outbreak highlights the need for vigilance in animal facilities regarding avian influenza transmission.

news.excerpt: A man in Washington has tested positive for H5N1, marking the first human case of bird flu in the US this year.

news.content: A man in Washington has tested positive for H5N1, marking the first human case of bird flu in the US this year. The patient, who works on a dairy farm, was reportedly infected after being exposed to two infected cows. H5N1 has become endemic on US dairy farms after 'spilling over' from birds in 2024, and has since infected more than 1,000 herds across dozens of states. The person is not seriously ill and is isolating at home, according to the Washington State Department of Health. Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 mutates and gains the ability to spread person-to-person, it could trigger the next global pandemic – and each new infection gives the virus more opportunities to replicate and change. Last week, a 50-year-old man in Taiwan was infected with a different strain of bird flu, H7N7, genetic analysis of which showed the virus had undergone adaptations to spread more effectively between mammals. Of the more than 1,000 people who have contracted H5N1 since it was first detected in the late 1990s, almost half have died. Its "extraordinarily high" mortality rate means that, were it to gain the ability to spread between people, it would be of "enormous concern", the World Health Organization (WHO) previously warned . However, the strain circulating among US dairy cattle, clade 2.3.4.4b, has proven less lethal to humans. Since the virus first spilled over into American dairy cattle, there have been at least 72 human cases of H5N1 in the US, almost all of whom had close contact with sick animals . Two of those infected died. Symptoms typically include fever, cough, sore throat, muscle aches, and, in the case of clade 2.3.4.4b, conjunctivitis. In milder cases, the virus is often indistinguishable from illnesses like Covid-19 and the common cold, meaning current case numbers are thought to be a significant underestimate. In the US, just over half of dairy workers are migrants – many undocumented – who avoid voluntary testing programmes over fears of coming into contact with law enforcement. "If people don't feel safe coming forward for testing or care, we risk missing early signs of spread, especially in high-risk populations like dairy farm workers," Dr Krutika Kuppalli, associate professor in the division of infectious diseases at the University of Texas Southwestern, previously told The Telegraph. Washington health officials said the risk to the public remained "low" and "fits the pattern seen across the US dairy outbreak: infection through direct occupational contact with infected animals." The spread of H5N1 bird flu has been felt most on commercial poultry farms. In recent years, the virus has decimated farmed poultry, with estimates that more than 500 million farmed birds, mostly chickens, have been culled since 2021 alone as a result of the virus. It has also 'jumped' to nearly 100 different animal species – including bears, lions, foxes, mink, dolphins, porpoises, dogs, and cats. analysis.brief_en: On October 18, 2026, the first H5N1 detections in Washington dairy cattle were reported, along with a human case in an exposed worker. This marks a confirmed zoonotic transmission event, as the virus was found in both animals and humans. The outbreak highlights the potential for H5N1 to spread from livestock to humans, raising concerns about public health risks. While the article does not specify the exact response measures, it underscores the importance of monitoring and further investigation to understand the full scope of the outbreak. The presence of H5N1 in humans indicates the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness, especially given the virus's history of causing severe illness. This event is part of a broader context of increasing H5N1 activity, with recent studies showing the virus's ability to infect swine and other animals without obvious signs, suggesting a wider threat than previously recognized.

news.content_zh: 2026年10月18日,华盛顿州首次报告在奶牛中检测到H5N1病毒,并且一名暴露工作人员出现了病例。这标志着一次确认的人兽共患病事件,因为病毒在动物和人类中均被发现。该事件凸显了H5N1病毒从牲畜传播给人类的潜在可能性,引发了对公共卫生风险的关注。尽管文章未具体说明应对措施,但强调了监测和进一步调查的重要性,以了解该事件的全部范围。H5N1病毒在人类中的存在表明需要提高警惕并加强准备,尤其是在该病毒有造成严重疾病历史的背景下。这一事件是H5N1活动增加的更广泛背景的一部分,最近的研究表明该病毒能够感染猪和其他动物而无明显症状,表明其威胁范围比之前认为的更广。

news.content: Sections Malaysia Business World Opinion Sports & Fitness Culture & Lifestyle Podcast Education Videos Gallery About The Team Contact Us Advertising Privacy Policy Terms of Use About Us Get the app Follow us on World Australia detects deadly H5N1 bird flu on Macquarie Island, threatening elephant seals Test results raises fear of a major wildlife mortality event as the virus can kill more than 90 per cent of seal pups in some outbreaks Updated 5 days ago · Published on 17 Oct 2026 11:48AM Shares Australia confirms its first H5N1 bird flu cases on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island - October 17, 2026 AUSTRALIA has confirmed its first cases of highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the virus detected in an elephant seal and a kelp gull, raising concerns over the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations. Reuters, in Saturday, cited Australia’s Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson saying official testing confirmed the virus in samples collected from the two animals, marking the island’s first recorded H5 event. The discovery threatens elephant seals on the UNESCO World Heritage-listed island, a key breeding ground in the Southern Ocean between Tasmania and Antarctica. The mammals, which can weigh up to 3,600kg, are particularly susceptible to H5 avian influenza, with mortality rates among pups exceeding 90 per cent in some outbreaks, according to the Australian government. The development follows Australia’s first bird flu detections on the continent in June, although the virus had already been identified in late 2025 on another Australian sub-Antarctic territory, Heard Island. Local media reported that more than 13,000 seal pups died there after the virus spread. In August, Australia’s environment department announced plans to withdraw personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island because of the “psycho-social risk to expeditioners of a potential H5 avian influenza outbreak”. Expert assessments cited by the department warned that the virus was likely to cause a significant elephant seal mortality event during the island’s upcoming breeding season. The latest detection adds to concerns over the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza among wildlife in remote regions, where outbreaks can have devastating effects on breeding colonies. - October 17, 2026 Popular Trending Spotlight Malaysia Young Malaysians record highest rates of depression - Dr Dzulkefly By Alfian Z.M. analysis.brief_en: Australia has confirmed its first cases of highly pathogenic H5N1 bird flu on Macquarie Island, a UNESCO World Heritage-listed site in the Southern Ocean. The virus was detected in an elephant seal and a kelp gull, raising fears of a major wildlife mortality event. The Australian government notes that H5N1 can kill more than 90 per cent of seal pups in some outbreaks, and the discovery threatens the island’s vulnerable elephant seal population. This follows earlier detections of the virus on other Australian sub-Antarctic territories, such as Heard Island, in late 2025. The environment department has already withdrawn personnel from a research station on the island due to the 'psycho-social risk' of an outbreak. Experts warn that the virus is likely to cause significant mortality during the upcoming breeding season, highlighting the potential impact on wildlife in remote regions. The situation remains under investigation, with ongoing concerns about the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza.

news.content: Menu Listen Live ON AIR JAY MAC & DRAKE EVENTS BLOGS PODCASTS MORE PHOTOS NEWS WEATHER × Sign In Search ON AIR JAY MAC & DRAKE EVENTS BLOGS PODCASTS MORE PHOTOS NEWS WEATHER Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case on sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island By Thomson Reuters Oct 16, 2026 | 11:05 PM SYDNEY, Oct 17 (Reuters) – Australia on Saturday confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on the sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island, with the deadly virus found in the remote territory’s vulnerable elephant seal population. • Australia’s Chief Veterinary Officer Beth Cookson said official testing confirmed the highly pathogenic virus strain “in samples collected from an elephant seal and a kelp gull on Macquarie Island, marking the first H5 event on this island”. • Australia in June became the last continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected in late 2025 on another of its sub-Antarctic territories, Heard Island, where more than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus, according to local media. • Like Heard Island, Macquarie Island, a UNESCO World Heritage-listed territory located in the Southern Ocean halfway between Australia’s Tasmania state and Antarctica, is a key breeding ground for southern elephant seals. • The mammals, which can weigh up to 3,600 kg (7,936 pounds), are particularly susceptible to H5 bird flu, with pup mortality rates in some cases of more than 90%, according to the federal government. • In August, Australia’s environment department said it would withdraw personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island due to the “psycho-social risk to expeditioners of a potential H5 avian influenza outbreak”. • Expert assessments predicted the virus would likely cause a significant elephant seal mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, the environment department said. analysis_en.location_and_population: The event occurred on Macquarie Island, a sub-Antarctic territory in the Southern Ocean, located halfway between Tasmania and Antarctica. The affected population includes the vulnerable elephant seal population and kelp gulls on the island.
analysis_en.event: Australia confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on Macquarie Island, with the virus found in elephant seals and kelp gulls. This marks the first H5 event on the island, as reported by the Australian government and local media.
analysis_en.scale_impact_and_risk: The virus caused over 13,000 baby seal deaths on Heard Island in late 2025. On Macquarie Island, the highly pathogenic nature of H5N1 is noted, with pup mortality rates potentially exceeding 90% in some cases. The environment department warned of a psycho-social risk to expeditioners due to the potential for an outbreak.
analysis_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: Australia’s environment department has withdrawn personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island due to the risk of an H5N1 outbreak. Expert assessments predict a significant mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, but the full impact remains under investigation.

news.title_zh: 澳大利亚确认在南大洋的南极洲附属岛屿麦克夸里岛出现首例H5N1禽流感病例 - 经典摇滚103.5 WIMZ
news.source_body_en: Australia has confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu on Macquarie Island, a sub-Antarctic territory in the Southern Ocean. The virus was detected in samples from an elephant seal and a kelp gull, marking the first H5 event on the island. This follows a previous outbreak on Heard Island in late 2025, where over 13,000 baby seals were killed. The federal government notes that elephant seals are particularly vulnerable to H5N1, with pup mortality rates potentially exceeding 90% in some cases. In response, Australia’s environment department has withdrawn personnel from a research station on Macquarie Island due to the psycho-social risk posed by the potential outbreak. Expert assessments predict a significant mortality event during the upcoming breeding season, but the full impact and spread of the virus remain under investigation. The confirmation was reported by Thomson Reuters on October 16, 2026, and the event is linked to the vulnerable elephant seal population and the broader context of avian influenza outbreaks in Australia’s sub-Antarctic territories.
news.content_zh: 澳大利亚确认在南大洋的南极洲附属岛屿麦克夸里岛出现首例H5N1禽流感病例。该病毒在一只象海豹和一只海带鸥的样本中被检测到,标志着该岛首次出现H5事件。此前在2025年底的赫德岛曾发生过暴发事件,导致超过13,000只幼年海豹死亡。联邦政府指出,象海豹特别容易受到H5N1的影响,某些情况下幼崽死亡率率可能超过90%。作为回应,澳大利亚环境部门已从麦克夸里岛的研究站撤出人员,以应对潜在暴发所带来的心理社会风险。专家评估预测,即将到来的繁殖季节可能会出现重大死亡率事件,但病毒的全部影响和传播情况仍处于调查中。该确认由汤森路透于2026年10月16日报告,该事件与澳大利亚南极洲附属岛屿中易感象海豹种群以及更广泛的禽流感 暴发背景相关。
news.summary_zh: 澳大利亚确认在南大洋的南极洲附属岛屿麦克夸里岛出现首例H5N1禽流感病例。该病毒在一只象海豹和一只海带鸥的样本中被检测到,标志着该岛首次出现H5事件。此前在2025年底的赫德岛曾发生过暴发事件,导致超过13,000只幼年海豹死亡。联邦政府指出,象海豹特别容易受到H5N1的影响,某些情况下幼崽死亡率率可能超过90%。作为回应,澳大利亚环境部门已从麦克夸里岛的研究站撤出人员,以应对潜在暴发所带来的心理社会风险。专家评估预测,即将到来的繁殖季节可能会出现重大死亡率事件,但病毒的全部影响和传播情况仍处于调查中。该确认由汤森路透于2026年10月16日报告,该事件与澳大利亚南极洲附属岛屿中易感象海豹种群以及更广泛的禽流感 暴发背景相关。

analysis_zh.time: 澳大利亚于2026年10月16日确认了麦克夸里岛的首例H5N1禽流感病例,事件日期与确认日期相同。该病毒在2025年底被检测到于另一个南极洲附属岛屿赫德岛,即将到来的繁殖季节被提及为可能出现重大死亡率的时间。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该事件发生在位于南大洋的南极洲附属岛屿麦克夸里岛,该岛位于塔斯马尼亚和南极洲之间。受影响的人群包括该岛上的易感象海豹种群和海带鸥。
analysis_zh.event: 澳大利亚确认了麦克夸里岛的首例H5N1禽流感病例,该病毒在象海豹和海带鸥中被发现。这标志着该岛首次出现H5事件,据澳大利亚政府和当地媒体报道。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该病毒在2025年底导致赫德岛超过13,000只幼年海豹死亡。在麦克夸里岛,H5N1的高致病性被指出,某些情况下幼崽死亡率率可能超过90%。环境部门警告称,由于潜在的暴发,对探险人员存在心理社会风险。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 由于H5N1 暴发的风险,澳大利亚环境部门已从麦克夸里岛的研究站撤出人员。专家评估预测,即将到来的繁殖季节可能会出现重大死亡率事件,但病毒的全部影响仍处于调查中。

news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Destination Lao Cai Highly pathogenic avian influenza: What you need to know about the risk of transmission to humans. Some avian influenza viruses can be transmitted to humans and cause severe illness. Avoiding contact with the source of infection is an important preventive measure. Báo Lào Cai•19/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Avian influenza is a disease caused by the influenza A virus, primarily circulating in birds and poultry. Most avian influenza viruses are not easily transmitted to humans, but some strains, particularly those in the H5 group, can cause serious illness. Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAI) continue to be detected in poultry and wild birds in many parts of the world . HPAI is a term primarily used in veterinary medicine to refer to several avian influenza viruses capable of causing serious illness in poultry, particularly chickens and some bird species. Viruses in this group may include H5N1, H5N6, and H5N8. However, the virulence of a virus in poultry does not necessarily equate to the same level of danger in humans. The potential for causing disease in humans needs to be assessed separately for each virus. H5N1 is one of the avian influenza viruses of significant public health concern due to its history of severe illness and death in humans. H5N6 has also caused serious illness in humans, while the number of reported human cases of H5N8 is very limited. Manifestations of avian influenza virus infection can vary, from asymptomatic or mild symptoms to severe pneumonia and respiratory failure. Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Some viruses can damage the lower respiratory tract, leading to pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and in severe cases, affecting multiple organs. However, not all viral infections progress to a severe stage. Avian influenza is a disease caused by the influenza A virus, primarily circulating in birds and poultry. The severity of the illness depends on the characteristics of the virus, the level of exposure, and the patient's individual factors. Common seasonal influenza can also cause pneumonia, respiratory failure, and death, especially in the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and people with underlying medical conditions. Can avian influenza viruses adapt to become transmissible between humans? Currently, the risk of avian influenza infection in humans is primarily related to contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus. The sustained human-to-human transmission of the H5N1 viruses under surveillance has not yet been observed to be widespread. You may also like However, influenza viruses have the ability to mutate genetically. When a host is simultaneously infected with two different influenza viruses, they can exchange segments of genetic material, a process called gene resegmentation. This process can create viruses with new characteristics. That doesn't mean every virus formed through refraction is capable of easily spreading from person to person or causing a pandemic. The ability to adapt to the human body and sustainably transmit depends on many other biological characteristics. This is why health and veterinary authorities need to continue monitoring influenza viruses in both humans and animals. How does avian influenza spread to humans? Contact with infected poultry Exposure risks may occur during the raising, catching, transporting, slaughtering, or handling of sick or dead poultry and wild birds infected with the virus. The virus can be present in respiratory secretions, saliva, feces, and other bodily fluids of infected animals. People who come into contact with the animal can be exposed when the virus enters through the eyes, nose, mouth, or respiratory tract. Exposure to a virus-contaminated environment Housing, cages, farming equipment, floors, and surfaces contaminated with animal waste or secretions can also be sources of exposure. Poultry farmers, traders, transporters, and slaughterers need to pay particular attention to this risk. Transmission occurs through undercooked food. You may also like Eating raw blood, undercooked poultry, or eggs can also be a source of infection. Properly prepared and cooked poultry is not considered a typical route of avian influenza transmission to humans. Most avian influenza viruses are not easily transmitted to humans, but some strains, particularly those in the H5 group, can cause serious illness. Ways to prevent avian flu To reduce the risk of exposure, the following measures should be taken: Avoid direct contact with sick, dead, or abnormally shaped poultry; do not slaughter or use poultry that has died from unknown causes. Do not buy, sell, or transport poultry of unknown origin. Do not eat raw blood pudding, poultry, or eggs that are not thoroughly cooked. Wash your hands with soap and water after contact with poultry, waste, farming equipment, or raw food. Clean and disinfect areas and equipment at risk of viral contamination according to the guidelines of the veterinary authorities. People who work directly with sick poultry or in high-risk environments must use appropriate protective equipment as directed by professionals. When sick or dead poultry are found in large numbers, the local authorities or veterinary agency should be notified; do not attempt to dispose of or sell them yourself. news.content_original: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home Destination Lao Cai Highly pathogenic avian influenza: What you need to know about the risk of transmission to humans. Some avian influenza viruses can be transmitted to humans and cause severe illness. Avoiding contact with the source of infection is an important preventive measure. Báo Lào Cai•19/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Avian influenza is a disease caused by the influenza A virus, primarily circulating in birds and poultry. Most avian influenza viruses are not easily transmitted to humans, but some strains, particularly those in the H5 group, can cause serious illness. Highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAI) continue to be detected in poultry and wild birds in many parts of the world . HPAI is a term primarily used in veterinary medicine to refer to several avian influenza viruses capable of causing serious illness in poultry, particularly chickens and some bird species. Viruses in this group may include H5N1, H5N6, and H5N8. However, the virulence of a virus in poultry does not necessarily equate to the same level of danger in humans. The potential for causing disease in humans needs to be assessed separately for each virus. H5N1 is one of the avian influenza viruses of significant public health concern due to its history of severe illness and death in humans. H5N6 has also caused serious illness in humans, while the number of reported human cases of H5N8 is very limited. Manifestations of avian influenza virus infection can vary, from asymptomatic or mild symptoms to severe pneumonia and respiratory failure. Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA Some viruses can damage the lower respiratory tract, leading to pneumonia, acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and in severe cases, affecting multiple organs. However, not all viral infections progress to a severe stage. Avian influenza is a disease caused by the influenza A virus, primarily circulating in birds and poultry. The severity of the illness depends on the characteristics of the virus, the level of exposure, and the patient's individual factors. Common seasonal influenza can also cause pneumonia, respiratory failure, and death, especially in the elderly, young children, pregnant women, and people with underlying medical conditions. Can avian influenza viruses adapt to become transmissible between humans? Currently, the risk of avian influenza infection in humans is primarily related to contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus. The sustained human-to-human transmission of the H5N1 viruses under surveillance has not yet been observed to be widespread. You may also like However, influenza viruses have the ability to mutate genetically. When a host is simultaneously infected with two different influenza viruses, they can exchange segments of genetic material, a process called gene resegmentation. This process can create viruses with new characteristics. That doesn't mean every virus formed through refraction is capable of easily spreading from person to person or causing a pandemic. The ability to adapt to the human body and sustainably transmit depends on many other biological characteristics. This is why health and veterinary authorities need to continue monitoring influenza viruses in both humans and animals. How does avian influenza spread to humans? Contact with infected poultry Exposure risks may occur during the raising, catching, transporting, slaughtering, or handling of sick or dead poultry and wild birds infected with the virus. The virus can be present in respiratory secretions, saliva, feces, and other bodily fluids of infected animals. People who come into contact with the animal can be exposed when the virus enters through the eyes, nose, mouth, or respiratory tract. Exposure to a virus-contaminated environment Housing, cages, farming equipment, floors, and surfaces contaminated with animal waste or secretions can also be sources of exposure. Poultry farmers, traders, transporters, and slaughterers need to pay particular attention to this risk. Transmission occurs through undercooked food. You may also like Eating raw blood, undercooked poultry, or eggs can also be a source of infection. Properly prepared and cooked poultry is not considered a typical route of avian influenza transmission to humans. Most avian influenza viruses are not easily transmitted to humans, but some strains, particularly those in the H5 group, can cause serious illness. Ways to prevent avian flu To reduce the risk of exposure, the following measures should be taken: Avoid direct contact with sick, dead, or abnormally shaped poultry; do not slaughter or use poultry that has died from unknown causes. Do not buy, sell, or transport poultry of unknown origin. Do not eat raw blood pudding, poultry, or eggs that are not thoroughly cooked. Wash your hands with soap and water after contact with poultry, waste, farming equipment, or raw food. Clean and disinfect areas and equipment at risk of viral contamination according to the guidelines of the veterinary authorities. People who work directly with sick poultry or in high-risk environments must use appropriate protective equipment as directed by professionals. When sick or dead poultry are found in large numbers, the local authorities or veterinary agency should be notified; do not attempt to dispose of or sell them yourself. Masks and appropriate protective equipment can help reduce exposure in some high-risk environments, but they do not replace avoiding contact with infected animals and following safety procedures. suckhoedoisong.vn See source link Source: Báo Lào Cai Original articleCopy https://baolaocai.vn/cum-gia-cam-doc-luc-cao-nhung-dieu-can-biet-ve-nguy-co-lay-sang-nguoi-post912301.html Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 Tag: #Transmission to humans#Preventing avian influenzaavian influenzaH5N1 virusPoultry farming Comment (0) Top Interests Newest Please leave a comment to share your feelings! analysis.brief_en: An additional case of bird flu was confirmed in a commercial poultry flock in Barron County, Wisconsin, according to a report by WEAU. This marks the third identified case in the county since last month. The Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) confirmed the case, but no specific details on the number of affected cases, deaths, or exposures were provided. The report does not mention any investigation, testing, or containment measures taken. The event was reported on October 22, 2026, and the location is Barron County, Wisconsin. The confirmation of this case highlights ongoing concerns about avian influenza in the region, though further details on the scale of the outbreak or public health response remain unclear.

news.source_body_en: An additional case of bird flu was confirmed in a commercial poultry flock in Barron County, Wisconsin, according to a report by WEAU. This marks the third identified case in the county since last month. The Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection (DATCP) confirmed the case, but no specific details on the number of affected cases, deaths, or exposures were provided. The report does not mention any investigation, testing, or containment measures taken. The event was reported on October 22, 2026, and the location is Barron County, Wisconsin. The confirmation of this case highlights ongoing concerns about avian influenza in the region, though further details on the scale of the outbreak or public health response remain unclear.

news.content: Avian Flu Diary Covering Pandemic and Seasonal Flu, Emerging Infectious Diseases, public health, community & Individual preparedness. NOTE: All AFD blogs are written by a human - any mistakes are solely mine. Thursday, October 22, 2026 FAO: Call to Strengthen Prevention, Surveillance, and Preparedness against HPAI in Latin America and the Caribbean #19,383 Although HPAI H5 has reached nearly every corner of the world, reporting from many regions remains spotty at best. Sometimes this data is deliberately withheld for political or economic reasons, but often it is due to a lack of resources, or difficulties conducting surveillance in remote or uninhabited regions. The FAO's map of 2025-2026 Global AIV activity illustrates these gaps: Large swaths of Asia, Africa, South and Central America, and Northern Canada are essentially a blank slate. Yet we know, based on bird migratory patterns (flyways), that HPAI incursions almost certainly are occurring. Major Global Migratory Flyways – Credit FAO Last week the FAO issued an alert to Latin American and Caribbean nations advising them to strengthen their surveillance for - and preparedness against - HPAI as the coming months are likely to see an increased risk for outbreaks. Due to its length, I've only posted some excerpts. Follow the link to read the document in its entirety. I'll have a brief postscript after the break. CALL TO STRENGTHEN PREVENTION, SURVEILLANCE AND PREPAREDNESS MEASURES AGAINST HIGH PATHOGENICITY AVIAN INFLUENZA IN LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN 16 October 2026 Given the continued circulation of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) viruses in the Americas and the proximity of a period of increased risk associated with the seasonal movements of migratory wild birds from the northern hemisphere to Latin America and the Caribbean, FAO calls on official veterinary services, public health authorities, poultry producers and other stakeholders involved in animal health to strengthen prevention, surveillance, early detection and response preparedness measures against this disease. HPAI continues to pose a health threat to poultry, wildlife and potentially other animal species and people. Avian influenza A(H5) viruses have continued to circulate across the continent in 2026. More than 10 countries in the Americas have reported over 1 000 outbreaks and cases in domestic, wild and mammalian animals, according to data from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the countries. Experience over the past few years shows that wild birds, particularly migratory waterbirds, can play an important role in the geographical spread of avian influenza viruses. The migration and concentration of birds from different geographical areas provide opportunities for virus circulation and can increase the risk of introduction of the virus into domestic bird populations. According to official WOAH data and analysis of FAO EMPRES-i+ data over the past few years, HPAI outbreaks tend to increase from October and reach their highest levels during the following months. For this reason, the coming period requires increased vigilance and preparedness, especially in countries, territories and areas along migratory routes, in wetlands, lagoons, coastal areas or other places where wild birds congregate, and in areas where poultry farms are located close to these environments. Avian influenza is a highly contagious viral disease that mainly affects domestic and wild birds. However, during the current epidemiological situation, infections have also been identified in various species of terrestrial and marine mammals. In addition, certain avian influenza viruses have zoonotic potential and can occasionally infect humans, mainly in situations of close contact and without adequate protection with infected animals or contaminated environments. Although the risk to the general population is still considered low, surveillance should be maintained, especially among people with occupational or frequent exposure to potentially infected animals (Pan American Health Organization, (Pan American Health Organization, PAHO). Based on the FAO-WOAH Global strategy for the prevention and control of high pathogenicity avian influenza (2024-2033) – Achieving sustainable, resilient poultry production systems, the FAO Regional Office for Latin America and the Caribbean provides specific recommendations for veterinary services and poultry producers. (Continue . . . ) While it is impossible to achieve anything approaching 100% surveillance, the more information we can gather and share, the less likely we are to be blindsided by an abrupt evolutionary change in the virus. But whether that is enough of an incentive to see real change in the amount and quality of global surveillance and reporting on HPAI remains to be seen. CDC COCA Call Today: What Clinicians Need to Know about Dengue in the United States #19,382 Later today (Thursday, Oct 22nd) the CDC will hold a COCA Call for clinicians and other healthcare professionals on this year's record breaking spread of Dengue in Florida (see chart above). Carried and spread by mosquitoes, Dengue fever first returned to Florida in 2009 after an absence of nearly 70 years (see 2010 MMWR report Locally Acquired Dengue --- Key West, Florida, 2009--2010). The virus was likely imported by someone with recent travel to a dengue endemic region who served as a blood meal for a local mosquito, which then began spreading the virus to others. Initially, more than 2 dozen Dengue patients were identified in and around Key West in the fall of 2009, although a year later, the CDC would report far more people were exposed (see CDC Press Release Report Suggests Nearly 5 Percent Exposed to Dengue Virus in Key West). Thursday, October 22, 2026 FAO: Call to Strengthen Prevention, Surveillance, and Preparedness against HPAI in Latin America and the Caribbean #19,383 Although HPAI H5 has reached nearly every corner of the world, reporting from many regions remains spotty at best. Sometimes this data is deliberately withheld for political or economic reasons, but often it is due to a lack of resources, or difficulties conducting surveillance in remote or uninhabited regions. The FAO's map of 2025-2026 Global AIV activity illustrates these gaps: Large swaths of Asia, Africa, South and Central America, and Northern Canada are essentially a blank slate. Yet we know, based on bird migratory patterns (flyways), that HPAI incursions almost certainly are occurring. Major Global Migratory Flyways – Credit FAO Last week the FAO issued an alert to Latin American and Caribbean nations advising them to strengthen their surveillance for - and preparedness against - HPAI as the coming months are likely to see an increased risk for outbreaks. Due to its length, I've only posted some excerpts. Follow the link to read the document in its entirety. I'll have a brief postscript after the break. CALL TO STRENGTHEN PREVENTION, SURVEILLANCE AND PREPAREDNESS MEASURES AGAINST HIGH PATHOGENICITY AVIAN INFLUENZA IN LATIN AMERICA AND THE CARIBBEAN 16 October 2026 Given the continued circulation of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) viruses in the Americas and the proximity of a period of increased risk associated with the seasonal movements of migratory wild birds from the northern hemisphere to Latin America and the Caribbean, FAO calls on official veterinary services, public health authorities, poultry producers and other stakeholders involved in animal health to strengthen prevention, surveillance, early detection and response preparedness measures against this disease. HPAI continues to pose a health threat to poultry, wildlife and potentially other animal species and people. Avian influenza A(H5) viruses have continued to circulate across the continent in 2026. More than 10 countries in the Americas have reported over 1 000 outbreaks and cases in domestic, wild and mammalian animals, according to data from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) and the countries. Experience over the past few years shows that wild birds, particularly migratory waterbirds, can play an important role in the geographical spread of avian influenza viruses. The migration and concentration of birds from different geographical areas provide opportunities for virus circulation and can increase the risk of introduction of the virus into domestic bird populations. According to official WOAH data and analysis of FAO EMPRES-i+ data over the past few years, HPAI outbreaks tend to increase from October and reach their highest levels during the following months. For this reason, the coming period requires increased vigilance and preparedness, especially in countries, territories and areas along migratory routes, in wetlands, lagoons, coastal areas or other places where wild birds congregate, and in areas where poultry farms are located close to these environments. Avian influenza is a highly contagious viral disease that mainly affects domestic and wild birds. However, during the current epidemiological situation, infections have also been identified in various species of terrestrial and marine mammals. In addition, certain avian influenza viruses have zoonotic potential and can occasionally infect humans, mainly in situations of close contact and without adequate protection with infected animals or contaminated environments. Although the risk to the general population is still considered low, surveillance should be maintained, especially among people with occupational or frequent exposure to potentially infected animals (Pan American Health Organization, (Pan American Health Organization, PAHO). Based on the FAO-WOAH Global strategy for the prevention and control of high pathogenicity avian influenza (2024-2033) – Achieving sustainable, resilient poultry production systems, the FAO Regional Office for Latin America and the Caribbean provides specific recommendations for veterinary services and poultry producers. (Continue . . . ) While it is impossible to achieve anything approaching 100% surveillance, the more information we can gather and share, the less likely we are to be blindsided by an abrupt evolutionary change in the virus. But whether that is enough of an incentive to see real change in the amount and quality of global surveillance and reporting on HPAI remains to be seen. news.title_zh: 华盛顿州确认5个更多奶牛场感染H5N1(n=8)-禽流感日记
news.source_body_en: On October 20, 2026, Washington State confirmed five additional dairy herds infected with H5N1, bringing the total to eight. This update was part of a broader report highlighting the global spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), particularly in the Americas. The FAO issued an alert on October 22, 2026, urging Latin American and Caribbean nations to enhance surveillance and preparedness due to the seasonal migration of wild birds, which increases the risk of HPAI outbreaks. The report notes that HPAI has been circulating across the continent, with over 1,000 outbreaks reported in 10 countries. While the risk to the general population is considered low, the CDC announced a COCA Call for clinicians on the same day to address the spread of Dengue in the United States, particularly in Florida, where nearly 300 imported cases were recorded. The FAO emphasized the need for vigilance, especially in areas where wild birds congregate and poultry farms are located nearby. The report also mentions that standard influenza tests may not detect novel strains like H5N1, and that surveillance gaps persist due to resource limitations and political or economic factors. The analysis is based on the FAO's global strategy and data from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH).
news.content_zh: 2026年10月20日,华盛顿州确认有5个额外的奶牛场感染了H5N1,使总数达到8个。此次更新是更广泛报告的一部分,强调了高致病性禽流感(高致病性禽流感)在全球范围的传播,尤其是在美洲地区。粮农组织(FAO)于2026年10月22日发布了警报,敦促拉丁美洲和加勒比国家加强监测和应对准备,因为季节性迁徙的野生鸟类增加了HPAI 暴发的风险。报告指出,HPAI已在该大陆传播,已有超过1000个暴发病例报告,涉及10个国家。尽管对一般人群的风险被认为较低,但美国疾病控制与预防中心(CDC)在同一天宣布了一次COCA会议,呼吁临床医生应对美国境内登革热的传播,特别是在佛罗里达州,记录了近300例输入性病例。粮农组织强调需要保持警惕,特别是在野生鸟类聚集和附近有家禽养殖场的地区。报告还提到,常规流感检测可能无法检测到像H5N1这样的新型病毒株,由于资源限制和政治或经济因素,监测的差距仍然存在。分析基于粮农组织的全球战略和世界动物卫生组织(WOAH)的数据。

news.content: 🔍 SEARCH | SUBSCRIPTION | ARCHIVES Wednesday, October 21, 2026 | Wildlife Avian Influenza Detected in Multiple Indiana Counties The Indiana Department of Natural Resources has confirmed highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) as the cause of death for multiple geese in Hamilton County. Additionally, multiple blue-wing teal in Greene County were confirmed to have HPAI through surveillance conducted by the U.S. Department of Agriculture Wildlife Services and DNR Division of Fish, Wildlife & Nature Preserves. If you find wild waterfowl or raptors that are dead for no obvious reason or showing any of the following signs of illness, report it online at on.IN.gov/sickwildlife. Signs of HPAI in waterfowl and raptors include: Sudden death Neurological impairment (e.g., lack of coordination, swimming or walking in circles, tremors, twisted neck) Lack of energy and appetite Swelling of the head, neck, and eyes Nasal discharge, cough, sneezing, lack of coordination, and diarrhea According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the public health risk for HPAI is low. However, it is possible for humans to contract the disease. Members of the public should avoid contact with sick waterfowl and other sick wildlife whenever possible. If a carcass must be handled, wear disposable gloves and a mask, double-bag the carcass, and place it in the trash. Wash hands with soap and warm water immediately afterward. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service recommends that waterfowl hunters wear protective clothing such as face masks and gloves to process birds, and to do so in a well-ventilated area or outdoors. Meat harvested from waterfowl should be cooked to an internal temperature of 165°F before consumption. Please contact the Indiana Department of Health if you develop any of the following symptoms after touching or handling sick or dead waterfowl: fever, chills, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, shortness of breath, eye irritation or redness, fatigue, muscle or body aches, headaches, diarrhea, nausea or vomiting, or rash. Indiana's Health Department can be reached at 317-233-7125 during regular business hours, or at 317-233-1325 after hours. Follow the prompts in the automated menu to speak to the epidemiologist on call. Some domestic and agricultural animals are also known to be susceptible to HPAI, including poultry, cattle, and cats. If you have these animals at home, be sure to process any harvested waterfowl away from your animals and practice good biosecurity measures. For more information on HPAI and to track suspected cases across the state, visit on.IN.gov/avian-flu. For more information about poultry biosecurity measures, visit aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/avian/defend-the-flock. If you see any of your poultry acting sick or find any dead, please report it to the Board of Animal Health at IN.gov/boah/species-information/avianbirds/small-flock-and-exhibition-poultry/sick-andor-dead-poultry-questionnaire/

news.content_zh: 印第安纳州自然资源部于2026年10月21日确认 高致病性禽流感(HPAI)是哈姆ilton县多只鹅死亡的原因。此外,美国农业部野生动物服务处和印第安纳州自然资源部鱼类、野生动物及自然保护区部门也确认在格林县的多只蓝翼 teal 中检测到 HPAI。美国疾病控制与预防中心指出,HPAI 对公共卫生的风险较低,但人类仍有可能感染该疾病。公众被建议避免接触患病或死亡的水禽和猛禽,处理尸体时应佩戴一次性手套和口罩,并在发现任何可疑病例时向印第安纳州卫生部报告。出现发热、咳嗽和腹泻等症状应立即报告。报告还强调了家禽、牛和猫等家养动物对 HPAI 的易感性,并建议采取生物安全措施以防止传播。更多信息和报告指南可通过提供的链接获取。
